analysis.investment_thesis: CapitalNumbers ticks many SMILE boxes — 203 Cr small-cap, P/E 8.91, debt-free, 74.67% promoter holding, ROCE 26.5% — and sits in a large global digital-services TAM. However, revenue growth collapsed from 28% CAGR to just 2% in FY25 (98→100 Cr) with EBITDA also contracting, so I'd watch for a re-acceleration post-IPO deployment before sizing up.
key_strengths: Textbook small-cap: 203 Cr mcap + P/E 8.91 + ROCE 26.5% + zero debt
Fresh IPO capital (equity 67→171 Cr) gives dry powder for inorganic scale
key_risks: Growth stalling: revenue 93→98→100 Cr (only 2% in FY25), EBITDA 35→32
IT services is dollar- and client-concentration-sensitive; TAM large but commoditized
Investing CF -77 Cr in FY25 — execution risk on deploying IPO proceeds
red_flags: Revenue deceleration and operating income contraction in FY25 despite strong prior trajectory
Other income jumped to 6 Cr (treasury from IPO) flattering reported PAT
analysis.detailed_analysis: From a SMILE lens, this is genuinely interesting: 203 Cr market cap sits in my sweet spot, promoter holds 74.67% (big skin in the game), the balance sheet is debt-free with 171 Cr equity post-IPO, and ROE/ROCE of 20%/26.5% are best-in-class for IT services. Valuation at P/E ~9 is remarkably cheap versus midcap IT peers at 25-40x, and FCF has been positive all five years. The promoter just raised capital — that's ammunition for the "Large in aspiration" leg if they deploy it into acqui-hires or capability build-out in AI/digital engineering.\n\nWhat stops me from going beyond a 6 is the transformation catalyst is unproven. Revenue went 93→98→100 Cr — essentially flat for two years — and EBITDA contracted from 35 to 32 in FY25. A small-cap IT shop that has lost growth momentum is a value trap unless the post-IPO strategy re-ignites topline. The "E" (extra-large market) is real but CapitalNumbers is sub-scale in it. I'd watch 1-2 quarters for growth reacceleration, new client wins, and capital deployment before entering meaningfully — buy zone on any dip if FY26 H1 shows 20%+ growth returning.
